text: Simeon gives you a team of AI agents you can keep: teammates with names, faces, jobs, and context that builds over time. Each agent works on a cloud computer of its own, with a browser and files, so work gets finished in your real tools instead of ending as a chat draft. Get started with your first agent, or see what teams people build. You work with an agent by messaging it. Type, dictate, or call it. Give it a job, the context it needs, and access to the apps it uses. It takes on work that spans several apps and websites, keeps you updated in the chat, and comes back when something needs you

head: What makes Simeon different
text: - You start with Simeon, your chief of staff. Tell him what you need and he hires the right agent for it: a name, a face, a job title and a brief. You can also create agents yourself. - Each agent has a computer. Your agents work on a cloud computer with a browser and files. They use connected apps where they can and the browser for everything else, and their routines keep running while your Mac is closed. - Setup is a message, not a workflow builder. head: A good first handoff
text: Start with a real task that spans a few tools and has a clear finish line: Go through my inbox from this week. Reply to anything that only needs a yes or a date, flag what needs me, and put every invoice in the Finance folder in Google Drive. Ask me before sending anything to a client. This tells the agent what to do, where to work, what to leave for you, and where to stop. Review the result, correct it, and turn what works into a routine.

head: Does Simeon keep working when my Mac is closed?
text: Routines do. Your agents work on their own cloud computers, so a routine runs on schedule even when your Mac is asleep or closed. See Routines and skills.

head: Can several agents work at the same time?
text: Yes. Each agent has its own chat, its own job and its own computer, and they can hand work to each other.

head: What does an agent remember?
text: Your preferences, its job, and what it has learned about how you work. Your data stays in your account and is never used to train a model.

head: Can an agent use any website?
text: Agents can use most websites in their browser, including services without a connector. Some sites need a sign-in, a code or a human check; the agent then asks you to fill it in, or hands you the computer.

head: Which platforms are supported?
text: A Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 15 or later, and iPhone. Your agents and chats are the same on both.

head: How much does Simeon cost?
text: Standard is $30 a month, Pro $100 and Max $200, each with a 7-day free trial. See Plans and billing.

This guide takes you from install to your first finished task. You'll set up the Mac app, meet Simeon, hire your first agent and review its work.

head: Before you begin
text: You need a Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 15 or later. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial, so you can try Simeon before you pay; see Plans and billing.

head: 1. Install the Mac app
text: Download Simeon for macOS, open the file and drag Simeon into Applications. Then open it from Applications or Spotlight.

head: 2. Sign in
text: Choose Continue with Google , Continue with Apple , or sign in with your email and the code we send you. The same account works on the Mac and on iPhone. The app then sets up your agents' cloud computer and asks what your agents should call you. You can change your name later in Settings › Account .

head: 3. Meet Simeon
text: Simeon is your chief of staff. He introduces himself, then asks what you'd hand to a person if you hired one today. Answer in a sentence; he hires the right agent for it, with a name, a face, a job title and a brief. If you're not sure, ask him what he recommends. For a bigger project he proposes a small team, three agents at most to start.

head: 4. Give it a first task
text: Open the new agent's chat and type, or dictate. A strong request says what you want, which sources matter, what you want back, and where the agent should stop and check with you. For example: Find the five accounts we haven't heard from in a month, draft a short check-in for each in my voice, and show me the drafts before anything is sent.

head: 5. Connect the apps it needs
text: When the agent needs one of your apps, it shows a Connect card in the chat. Choose Connect , sign in on the app's own page, and you're done; the agent picks up where it left off. You can also connect apps ahead of time; see Connect apps.

head: 6. Review the result and make it stick
text: Check what the agent did, correct it, and tell it what to remember, like a report format or the hours you keep for meetings. When a task works well, turn it into a routine so it runs on its own. Before an agent sends an email, pays for something or posts anything, it asks you first. See Approvals, security, and privacy.

head: Use Simeon on your iPhone
text: The iPhone app connects to the same agents, chats and computers. Sign in with the same account to message your agents, call them, approve their requests and watch their computers. See Simeon for iPhone.

head: If something doesn't work
text: Most problems clear after you quit and reopen the app. For anything else, see the FAQ or contact us.

head: First tasks to try
text: Each of these is a good first message. Change the details to fit your work.

head: Inbox
text: Every morning, sort my inbox. Reply to anything that only needs a yes or a date, flag what needs me, and give me a short summary at 9.

head: Finance
text: Match this month's transactions in QuickBooks, chase any invoice more than 14 days late with a friendly reminder, and tell me where the money went.

head: Travel
text: Find me the cheapest refundable flight from Seattle to LA tomorrow, landing before 2pm. Show me the options before booking.

head: Social media
text: Turn what we shipped this week into three posts for Instagram and LinkedIn. Show me the drafts and schedule the ones I approve.

head: Research
text: Find the ten companies most likely to need what we sell, with the right person to contact at each and why.

head: Tips for a good brief
text: - One job per agent. "Inbox" and "Finance" work better as two agents than one "assistant". - Say where to stop. Tell the agent what it may do alone and what it should show you first. - Teach it once. Correct the first results and ask the agent to remember how you like things done.

Simeon for iPhone connects to the same agents, chats and computers as the Mac app. Sign in with the same account and everything is there. Simeon for iPhone isn't in the App Store yet. When it is, you'll find the download on simeonlabs.com.

head: What you can do on iPhone
text: - Message your agents. Type or dictate, attach photos, files and short videos. - Call an agent. Talk to it out loud; it works in the background while the call goes on. See Message and call your agents. - Approve or refuse. Approval cards show up in the chat and as notifications, so an agent is never stuck waiting for your desk. - Watch the computer and take control. Open an agent's computer to see its screen. Take control stops the agent at once and hands you the screen; give it back when you're done. See The agent's computer. - Connect apps. The same Connect button as on the Mac.

head: Requirements
text: An iPhone on iOS 26 or later.

head: Plans on iPhone
text: On iPhone, plans are bought through the App Store, with a 7-day free trial that needs no card. You manage or cancel the subscription in your Apple ID settings. See Plans and billing.
An agent is a teammate with one job: a name, a face, a job title, and a brief that says what it does and how. Each agent has its own chat and works on a cloud computer with a browser and files.

head: Hire through Simeon
text: Simeon is your chief of staff, the first agent on your team. Tell him what's taking up your week and he hires the right agent for it, with a name, a title that names the job, and a brief. He asks a question or two when the job isn't clear, then says what he assumed. I spend every Monday chasing invoices and updating our books. Can you hire someone for that? Hiring is Simeon's main job, but he can also keep everyone on track and take on work himself.

head: Create an agent yourself
text: Choose New Agent , then give it a name and describe the job in a sentence. The more specific the job, the better the agent: "Inbox" and "Finance" work better as two agents than one "assistant". You can also add a ready-made team from the Marketplace: five agents for your kind of work, already briefed.

head: Give it a face
text: Each agent gets a face. Open the agent's details to choose another, upload a picture, or generate one from a sentence.

head: Change an agent's job
text: Open the agent's details to rename it, change its title or rewrite its brief. You can also just tell it in the chat: "From now on, also handle our support inbox."

head: Work as a team
text: Agents can message each other and hand work along, so you aren't the router between them. Ask one agent to pass something to another, or let Simeon coordinate a bigger project.

You work with an agent the way you would with a colleague: in its chat, or on a call.

head: Messages
text: Type in the message field, or dictate. Give the agent the outcome you want, what matters, and where it should check with you. It replies as it works and tells you when it's done. - Mention an agent by name to point it out to another agent or bring it into the work. - Attach photos, files and short videos. An agent can read documents and say what happens in a video. - Files back. When an agent makes a file, it shows its name and kind in the chat; save or open it from there.

head: Drafts you can edit
text: When an agent writes an email or a Slack message for you, it can show it as a draft card. Edit the text in the card, then Send or Discard . Nothing goes out until you send it.

head: Questions and forms
text: When an agent needs a decision, it asks with a short question card. When a page on its computer needs something only you can type, like a sign-in or a one-time code, it asks with a form in the chat. You type in the card and the computer fills it in; a password or a code is masked, and the agent never sees what you typed.

head: Voice calls
text: Call an agent and talk to it out loud. It answers in a sentence or two and hands anything that needs doing to its work in the background, while the call goes on. Ask how it's going at any time.

head: Slack and Discord
text: An agent can also have its own Slack app or Discord bot, so your team can message it there and it answers there. You create the bot in Slack or Discord and give Simeon its token.

Each agent works on a cloud computer of its own, with a browser and files. That's why work gets finished in your real tools instead of ending as a chat draft: the agent can open a website, sign in, fill in a form, download a file and send it to you.

head: Watch it work
text: Open an agent's computer to see its screen live. You can keep working while it works; the chat tells you what it's doing.

head: Take control
text: Choose Take control to use the computer yourself. If the agent is working, it stops at once, so it never fights you for the mouse. When you're done, hand the computer back and the agent carries on. This is handy for a step only you can do, like a human check or a payment page you'd rather complete yourself.

head: Sign-ins and codes
text: When a page needs your sign-in, a one-time code or an address, the agent asks with a form in the chat instead of handing you the whole computer. Type in the card and the computer fills the page; a password or code is masked and never shown to the agent. Logins you save in the Credentials Store, and logins in 1Password if you connect it, can fill a sign-in for you after Face ID or Touch ID.

head: On your Mac
text: With your OK, an agent can also run commands and work with files on your Mac, as well as on its own computer. It asks first, and you choose Allow once , Always allow or Never ; you can change this later in Settings .

head: When your Mac is closed
text: Your agents' computers are in the cloud, so routines keep running on schedule while your Mac is asleep or closed.

Connectors let your agents work inside the apps you already use. There are more than 230, from Gmail, Slack and Notion to QuickBooks, HubSpot, Shopify and Figma. Browse them all in the connector directory.

head: Connect an app
text: Every app has one button, Connect , on the Mac and on iPhone. 1. Find the app in Connect apps , or choose Connect on the card an agent shows in the chat. 2. Confirm, then sign in on the app's own page. 3. The app shows as Connected . Your agents can use it right away. You sign in once; you never paste a password or an API key into Simeon. If you cancel the sign-in, nothing is left half-connected.

head: When an agent asks
text: You don't have to connect everything up front. When an agent needs an app it doesn't have yet, it shows a Connect card in the chat and continues once you've signed in.

head: Apps without a connector
text: Agents can still use most websites in their browser, on their own computer. A connector is faster and more reliable, so use one when it exists.

head: Your own servers
text: If you or your developers run an MCP server, you can add it by its address in Connect apps , and your agents can use its tools like any other connector.

head: Buying things for you
text: Two connectors let an agent buy what you asked for: - Link (by Stripe) pays with a one-time card, never your real one, and nothing is paid until you approve the purchase in the Link app. Link can also let an agent read the bank and card accounts you choose to share, to answer questions about your spending. - Shop (by Shopify) finds products across Shopify stores, pays with your Shop card, and tracks your orders. Every purchase shows a checkout card in the chat first, with Allow or Deny . See Approvals, security, and privacy.

head: Disconnect
text: Open the app in Connect apps to sign out or remove it. Your agents lose access at once.
A routine is a task an agent runs on its own: on a schedule, or when something happens. Because each agent works on its own cloud computer, routines keep running while your Mac is closed.

head: Set up a routine
text: Ask the agent in plain words: Every weekday at 8am, sort my inbox and send me a short summary of what needs me. The agent creates the routine and confirms when it will run. You can also make one yourself: open the agent, choose Routines , then New Routine , and give it a name, an instruction and when to run. Each routine has Active to turn it on or off, Test run to try it now, and Run history to see what it did. Delete removes it.

head: Run on an event
text: A routine can also start when something happens in another app, such as: - a mention in Slack , - a new pull request or a failed check in GitHub , - a new issue in Linear , - an error in Sentry , - an incident in PagerDuty . When someone mentions me in the support channel, draft a reply and show it to me.

head: Skills
text: A skill is a way of doing something that an agent can reuse, like your report format or your steps for onboarding a client. Teach an agent once and ask it to save the process as a skill. You can keep a skill to yourself or share it with your team, and it's added to every agent it's shared with.

head: Good routines
text: - Start with a task that already worked once in the chat, then make it a routine. - Say what to do with the result: send it to you, post it in Slack, or file it in Google Drive. - Keep approvals on for anything that sends, pays or posts. A routine still asks first.
The Credentials Store keeps the logins and details your agents need for sign-ins and sign-ups, without you typing them into the chat.

head: What you can save
text: Open Settings › Credentials Store on the Mac or iPhone. - Logins: a name, the website, the username or email, and the password. Add a hint like "use this for the supplier portal" to tell Simeon when to use it. - Contact info: your full name, email, phone and address, for forms and sign-ups. - Cards aren't kept here. Payments go through Link, which pays with a one-time card; see Connect apps. A saved password only shows after Face ID or Touch ID.

head: How a sign-in is filled
text: When a page on an agent's computer asks for a login you've saved, the agent asks to fill it. You confirm, and the computer types it in. The agent never sees the password.

head: 1Password
text: If you connect 1Password, the agent looks there first at a sign-in. A card asks you to Fill with 1Password , confirmed with Face ID or Touch ID, and the computer types the username, the password and the one-time code when the login has one.

head: Codes and anything else
text: For a one-time code sent to your phone, or anything not saved, the agent asks with a form in the chat. What you type is masked and goes straight to the page.
Your agents do the work, but nothing important happens without you.

head: What agents ask first
text: Before an agent sends an email, makes a payment or publishes something, it stops and asks in the chat. The approval card says what it wants to do and why, and you choose to allow or refuse it. The same goes for risky steps on its computer, like a command that would delete files. - Allow once lets this one action go ahead. - Always allow stops asking for that kind of action. - Refuse and the agent waits, or finds another way. Approval cards also come to your iPhone as notifications, so an agent isn't stuck while you're away from your desk.

head: Purchases
text: When an agent buys something for you through Link or Shop, a checkout card shows what it's buying, the total and the card that pays, with Allow (confirmed with Face ID) or Deny . Link pays with a one-time card, never your real one. See Connect apps.

head: Your data
text: - Encrypted at rest and in transit. - Isolated: each customer's data is kept apart from every other customer's. - Never used to train a model.

head: Passwords and codes
text: Agents never see your passwords or one-time codes. Sign-ins are filled from the Credentials Store or 1Password after Face ID or Touch ID, or typed by you in a masked form. You sign in to connected apps on their own pages, so Simeon never holds those passwords either.

head: Watch and step in
text: You can open an agent's computer at any time to watch it work, and Take control to stop it and take over. See The agent's computer.

head: Your Mac
text: An agent only runs commands or works with files on your Mac after you allow it. You can choose Never , and change your choice in Settings .
Every plan gives you the whole product: your agents, their computers, connectors, routines and voice calls. Plans differ in how much your agents can do each week.

head: Plans
text: Plan Price Usage each week --- --- --- Standard $30 a month The base allowance Pro $100 a month 3.5 times Standard Max $200 a month 9 times Standard, and earliest access to new products On the web, each plan is also sold yearly at 20% off. See Pricing.

head: Free trial
text: Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial. On the web it starts with a card and becomes your plan when the week ends, unless you cancel. On iPhone it needs no card. A trial includes one week of Standard usage, whichever plan you chose.

head: Usage
text: Your agents' work uses credits, and each plan gives you a number of credits a week. The week resets on its own. If you run out before it resets, you can wait, move to a bigger plan, or buy extra credits.

head: Extra credits
text: On a paid plan you can buy extra credits on the web: $10 for a pack. Extra credits are used only after the week's credits run out, and they last 12 months.

head: Change your plan
text: - Upgrade: starts today. You pay the new plan, less what's left of your current one, and get a fresh week. - Downgrade: takes effect at your next renewal; you keep your current plan until then.

head: Cancel
text: On the web, manage or cancel your subscription from your account's billing page. On iPhone, plans are bought through the App Store, so manage or cancel them in your Apple ID settings.

head: What is Simeon?
text: A team of AI agents for your business. Each agent has a job you give it, a computer of its own in the cloud, and access to the apps you already use. You ask in plain words, and they do the work.

head: Do I need to set anything up?
text: No. There are no workflows to build. Tell an agent what you need. When it needs one of your apps, it asks you to sign in once, on that app's own page.

head: Where does the work happen?
text: On each agent's own computer in the cloud, with a browser and files. You can watch it work or take over at any time, and routines keep running when your Mac is closed.

head: Will an agent act without asking?
text: Not on anything that matters. Before it sends an email, makes a payment or publishes something, it asks you in the chat, and you allow or refuse it.

head: Is my data safe?
text: Your data is encrypted, kept apart from every other customer, and never used to train a model. See Approvals, security, and privacy.

head: What do I need?
text: A Mac with Apple silicon on macOS 15 or later. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial.

head: How many agents can I have?
text: As many as your work needs. Your plan sets how much they can do each week, not how many there are.

head: Can my agents use apps that don't have a connector?
text: Yes. They can use most websites in their browser. A connector is faster and more reliable when there is one. See Connect apps.

head: Can I talk to an agent?
text: Yes. Call any agent and talk it through out loud. See Message and call your agents.

head: How do I cancel?
text: On the web, from your account's billing page; on iPhone, in your Apple ID settings. See Plans and billing.

head: Something isn't working
text: Quit and reopen the app first. If that doesn't fix it, contact us and tell us what you were doing.
